rv.q: Angela Carter hailed Kureishi’s novel for its humour and heart: this show comes with bundles of both.
What feels colourfully episodic as prose feels disjointed and scattershot here.
All this is played out in an unceasingly inventive carnival of theatre.

cn.t: Emma Rice's ebullient RSC adaptation of Hanif Kureishi's landmark novel wins praise for its inventive, playful energy and colorful staging, delivering an exuberant theatrical celebration of the provocative 1970s coming-of-age story.
